```plato

    //==
    // # Edge split
    //
    // Refinement. A per-edge decision array says which edges gain a midpoint; each
    // triangle then re-triangulates according to how many of its three edges were
    // chosen — the red-green refinement cases, 1-to-2, 1-to-3 and 1-to-4
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_refinement).
    //
    // The new vertices are APPENDED to the position array in edge order, so old
    // vertex numbers survive the pass unchanged. That is what lets Loop and
    // Butterfly subdivision below reuse this function for their topology and
    // simply supply a different position array of the same shape.

    // The vertex number of the midpoint introduced on each undirected edge, or -1
    // where the edge is not split. New vertices are numbered by the edge's rank
    // among the split edges, after the existing vertices.
    SplitVertexNumbers(splitMask: Array<Boolean>, baseVertexCount: Integer): Array<VertexIndex>
        => splitMask.Count.MapRange(e => VertexIndex(splitMask[e]
            ? baseVertexCount + e.MapRange(d => splitMask[d] ? 1 : 0).Reduce(0, (acc, hit) => acc + hit)
            : -1));
```
